arguments: Configuration check does not require a private-key type when asymmetric signing or key-agreement algorithms are enabled
message.text: Configuration check does not require a private-key type when asymmetric signing or key-agreement algorithms are enabled

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: valid because the checked configuration only requires asymmetric signing/key-agreement algorithm macros and does not require corresponding key-pair/private-key macros. Evidence: the key-module prerequisite list includes only public asymmetric key types at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:27, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:28, and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:29; the signing check requires only signing algorithms at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:81 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:91; and the key-derivation check treats ECDH/FFDH as key-agreement algorithms at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:101, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:103, and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_check_config.h:104. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Extend the configuration validation so modules that perform private-key operations require compatible private key-type macros, for example RSA/ECC key-pair types for signing and ECC/DH key-pair types for key agreement, or add explicit build-time errors tying each enabled asymmetric algorithm to its required key type(s). Also consider checking algorithm/key-type combinations rather than only requiring at least one algorithm per module.
properties.reasoning: The file validates that asymmetric signing and key-derivation modules have at least one corresponding algorithm enabled, but this check is not paired with any requirement that private key types needed to use those algorithms are enabled. The only key-type prerequisite check earlier in the file accepts public asymmetric key types only (`PSA_WANT_KEY_TYPE_ECC_PUBLIC_KEY`, `PSA_WANT_KEY_TYPE_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY`, `PSA_WANT_KEY_TYPE_DH_PUBLIC_KEY`) and does not mention private RSA/ECC/DH key types. In a cross-configuration where signing or ECDH/FFDH is compiled while private key-type support is omitted, the resulting firmware may have mismatched PSA crypto capability gating. Depending on surrounding dispatch code, that can become a privilege-boundary/configuration issue: clients may be exposed to operations whose key-type validation or backend support was not actually compiled, potentially leading to inconsistent authorization/denial behavior or latent unsafe error paths. The reviewed source does not prove runtime reachability, but the configuration validation is incomplete for private-key operations.
